title: Author every file beneath docs/ as AsciiDoc (.adoc), never markdown

facts.note: Location test: path under docs/ ending .md is the violation surface.
Generated output tree excluded by path, not by gitignore status.
Any committed .md present under docs/ (outside docs/dist/) is a finding; the validator scans the tree.
Planner tasks that will create or move documentation under docs/.

fires: A plan or wagon creates a new file such as docs/<area>/<topic>.md.
An existing markdown file is moved or copied into docs/ (outside docs/dist/).
The scan of docs/ finds any committed .md file not beneath docs/dist/.
doesNotFire: A .md file beneath docs/dist/ (generated build output, never scanned).
README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md or other markdown outside docs/, including the repository-root corpus.
A .adoc file authored anywhere beneath docs/.

given: A plan, wagon or doc change places an authored file beneath docs/ (any path not under docs/dist/).
when: The planner chooses the file's format or path.
then: The file MUST be AsciiDoc (.adoc); an authored .md beneath docs/ outside docs/dist/ is a violation.
prefer: Convert an existing docs/**/*.md to the same path with .adoc and keep its content intact.
When converting a historical document, place it INTO docs/archive/ and set its :status: accordingly; migration preserves history and never promotes it to current.
Decide by location only: under docs/, not under docs/dist/, ending .md → convert.
avoid: Committing authored markdown anywhere beneath docs/ outside docs/dist/.
Arguing a .md under docs/ is exempt because it is 'not really prose documentation' — the test is location, not content.
Treating conversion to .adoc as making a historical document current.
Expanding the plan to reject or convert README.md/CONTRIBUTING.md/root markdown under this rule; that belongs to the adoption step.
unless: The file is beneath docs/dist/ (generated output, never scanned).
The markdown is outside docs/ (e.g. README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, repository-root corpus); it is migrated by the adoption step, not rejected here.
why: A mixed corpus cannot carry the relationship graph: doc-id and :implements:/:supersedes: edges are AsciiDoc attributes and markdown has nowhere to put them, so format uniformity is the precondition for every other docs rule.
evidence: Validator scan of docs/ (excluding docs/dist/** by path) reports zero files ending .md.
Converted files exist at the same path with .adoc and preserved content; historical ones sit under docs/archive/ with a :status: attribute.
verifier_detail: Detector is a deterministic LOCATION test, not a content test: flag a path iff it is under docs/, not under docs/dist/, and ends .md. 'Is this really prose documentation?' is semantic and undecidable; the path test is deterministic and cheap (spec 2 §4 chose the decidable form on purpose; same reasoning as planner.docs.undeclared-change being the enforceable inverse of 'should this have been declared?').
Term authored_file: a file a human wrote and committed beneath docs/; anything under docs/ not under docs/dist/ is authored.
Term generated_output: everything beneath docs/dist/; rendered by the build (spec 2 §7), normally excluded from git, never subject to the authored-format rule.
Exclude docs/dist/** by path rather than by gitignore status, so the check is identical whether or not the tree has been built — this makes it deterministic in CI.
Markdown outside docs/ is out of scope for this detector.
Fix-hint example: docs/architecture/shared-control-root.md (✗ authored markdown under docs/) → docs/architecture/shared-control-root.adoc (✓ authored AsciiDoc).
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.
Source name: 'AsciiDoc is the only authored format beneath docs/'.
Lineage: the format half of the documentation model named in handoff spec 2 §4; it is an EXTENSION obligation because core is forbidden to know what a .adoc is (companion §4, Deliberately excluded).
Related rule references: planner.docs.graph-target-resolves (owns :implements:/:supersedes: edges), planner.docs.undeclared-change (same decidable-form reasoning).
Spec reference for archival conversion: spec 2 §2 Out of scope — migration preserves history and never promotes it.

sharedNodes.text: strict: atdd-bun fails on every finding; it has no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

additions.text: Do not expand the plan to convert README/CONTRIBUTING/root markdown under this rule.
